title: The Magic Water That Reflected Guilt
summary: A jewel thief hides among thirty palace servants. Birbal uses a bowl of ordinary spring water to make the culprit convict himself.
full_text:
A priceless ruby brooch belonging to the Queen vanished from the royal bedchamber. Thirty palace chambermaids and attendants were detained, but all swore they had not touched the jewel.

Emperor Akbar summoned Birbal: 'I cannot torture thirty innocent women. How will you uncover which one took the brooch?'

Birbal requested that all thirty attendants assemble in the quiet, dim council room. In the center of the room, Birbal placed a wide, polished silver basin filled with crystal-clear spring water.

Birbal stood beside the basin and announced in a solemn, mysterious voice:

'In this holy water, I have dissolved a sacred herbal essence prepared by the sages of Varanasi. It has no smell, but possesses one miraculous property:

'When an innocent woman looks down into the water, her face appears bright, beautiful, and clear.

'However, when the woman who stole the Queen's ruby looks into the water, the surface will instantly boil with black foam, and her reflection will appear with the face of a grinning demon, marking her for the executioner!'

Birbal ordered each woman to walk forward alone, look directly into the water for three breaths, and return to her line.

Twenty-nine women walked forward with calm, steady steps, leaned over the silver basin, looked down into the water, and smiled in relief at their clear, peaceful reflections.

Finally, the thirtieth attendant stepped forward. Her knees trembled, her breath came in shallow gasps, and her eyes were wild with terror.

Terrified that the magic water would turn black and display her face as a demon, she approached the basin, squeezed her eyelids tightly shut, held her breath, and backed away without looking into the water at all!

Birbal immediately caught her wrist: 'Here is your thief!'

The maid shrieked, fell to her knees in tears, and pulled the Queen's ruby brooch from inside her bodice!

Akbar asked in wonder: 'How did you know, Birbal?'

Birbal smiled: 'Sire, the water was ordinary well water from the garden. Twenty-nine innocent women looked into it without fear. But this woman was so terrified of what the water would reveal that she squeezed her eyes shut, proving that guilt was already boiling inside her own conscience!'

Akbar marveled at Birbal's psychological genius and restored the brooch to the Queen.
moral: Truth fears no inspection; the guilty mind creates its own prison.
